details.label: Summary
details.text: A severe wind and hail risk may continue tonight into south-central South Dakota and vicinity, with downstream watch issuance possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A well established supercell has gradually transitioned into a small bowing complex across western SD over the past hour or two, with mainly measured severe wind gusts up to around 75-80 mph. Even with the onset of nocturnal cooling, a reservoir of rich low-level moisture (with upper 60s to low 70s surface dewpoints) and steep mid-level lapse rates are supporting a narrow corridor of strong instability per latest mesoanalysis estimates. It is plausible that the ongoing small bow will track east-southeastward along the instability axis into south-central SD over the next few hours while continuing to pose a threat for severe gusts and hail. Time-lagged HRRR/RRFS runs support this scenario, with some members showing significant gust potential (75+ mph) persisting with eastward extent. Therefore, downstream watch issuance is being considered for parts of southern SD and far northern NE before the 04Z expiration of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 569

details.label: Summary
details.text: Strong to severe thunderstorms may materialize between 02-05 UTC across northern Illinois into northern Indiana. These storms will pose a risk of large to very large hail and severe gusts. Trends will be monitored, and watch issuance may be needed

details.label: Discussion
details.text: The northwestern edge of the cold pool associated with the earlier passage of an MCS is becoming increasingly diffuse across northern IL based on recently surface observations with temperature warming back into the upper 70s and briefly into the 80s before the onset of nocturnal cooling. Aloft, westerly 700-500 mb flow has advected steep lapse rates eastward back into the region, which were well sampled by the recent DVN and ILN 00 UTC RAOBs. As a result, the thermodynamic environment is steadily destabilizing and becoming increasingly supportive of intense convection. (These soundings also sampled extreme buoyancy between 4000-5000 J/kg MLCAPE and weak inhibition around -50 J/kg.) Over the past few hours, a subtle disturbance has been tracked across IA, evident by weak mid-level ascent. This feature has been supporting weak attempts at convection across southern MN and western WI, and will likely promote additional attempts within the destabilizing air mass across far eastern IA into northern IL later this evening. Latest guidance suggests that convective initiation is likely between 02-05 UTC, and will likely be focused along and north of the residual outflow boundary. Initially discrete to semi-discrete cells may mature into supercells before storm interactions within the zone of ascent promote clustering and upscale growth. Large to very large hail will be possible given the ample buoyancy and around 40 knots of effective shear if initially discrete modes can be adequately sustained. Strong to severe winds also appear possible given the shallow nature of the residual cold pool across northern IL.
